text:
Anya (Sales): Quick Q from FinPay POC — they need to confirm: can we guarantee tenant traffic stays in eu-west-1 unless capacity constraints trigger fallback? Also need list of subprocessors touching traffic in that path and pricing delta for egress to eu vs fallback to us-west.

Sam P.: Short answer: yes with tenant pinning + geofence routing policy, but fallback is possible and is charged differently. I'll pull numbers.

Mike (SRE): Important: we consider 'fallback' when 95th percentile CPU util on pinned pool > 85% for 5m. Fallback path uses nearest compatible replica (could be us-west).

Ryan (Infra): Adding routing policy example — can enforce 'hard' pin (reject) or 'soft' pin (failover). Soft is default for POC. Example config:
```
routing:
  tenant_pin: soft
  preferred_regions: [eu-west-1]
  failover_order: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1, us-west-2]
```

Anya (Sales): Customer asked for hard pin. What's the compliance/legal impact + ops complexity?

Legal Bot: Hard pin increases risk of outage if region unavailable. Also requires subprocessors list for each region; may trigger DPA addenda for subprocessor disclosure. We can provide attestation for current subprocessor set but not absolute guarantees on future changes.

Sam P.: For pricing: egress differential ~ $0.012/token-equivalent for eu vs us fallback on our pricing model for their commit size. Also hard pin may require reserved capacity (Dedicated) — that'll be a separate cost line.

Eva (Customer): For FinPay POC, they need KMS in EU and certs — can we ensure KMS keys never leave eu-west-1 for tenant? Also any additional attestation for subprocessor access?

Ryan (Infra): We support regional KMS via customer-managed KMS (BYOK). Default Redwood-managed keys may live in control plane region, but data plane keys can be provisioned in-customer KMS in eu-west-1. Need to confirm with security for attestation text.

Mike (SRE): Ops note — if they want hard pin without Dedicated, our autoscaling may reject new requests when pinned pool exhausted; we'll provide 429s. That is often unacceptable for their SLA.

Anya (Sales): Action items: Sam to send egress cost calc + note on reserved capacity; Ryan to draft sample routing YAML and KMS attestation wording; Legal to prepare subprocessor snapshot. Target: send to customer by EOD tomorrow. @Sam P. @Ryan (Infra) @Legal Bot

Sam P.: On it. I'll attach numbers and a one-pager. :thumbsup:

Ryan (Infra): I'll drop sample YAML + a short ops runbook for hard pin behavior.

Legal Bot: Preparing subprocessor list snapshot (pdf) and note about change process. ETA EOD.

Anya (Sales): Thanks everyone :pray:
